brief.subject: Rental pricing deception draws $49.75 million FTC settlement
brief.headline: Big Landlord Pays $49.75 Million Over Deceptive Rental Pricing
brief.dek: The FTC and four states settle with Progress Residential, a payment processor pays $600,000, and Amazon's ad case gets new details.
brief.lede: Progress Residential and owner Pretium Partners will pay $49.75 million to settle FTC and state charges of deceptive rental pricing. The FTC calls it its largest enforcement action against a landlord.

sections.heading: Landlord Settles Rental Pricing Charges
bullets: $49.75 million: what Progress Residential and Pretium Partners will pay to settle FTC and state charges.
Four states joined the FTC in alleging that renters were misled by deceptive rental pricing.
Progress Residential is the largest U.S. manager of single-family rental homes, so many renters could be affected.
Renters should compare the advertised rent with the total costs in the lease before signing.

sections.heading: Payment Processor's 'Risk-Free' Cancellation Claims
bullets: $600,000: what Riverside Payments, Cascade Equipment Leasing and their operators will pay the FTC and Washington state.
Regulators say the firms falsely promised small businesses lower payment processing costs.
Merchants were promised 'risk-free' cancellation, but regulators say canceling was made nearly impossible.
Small business owners should get cancellation terms in writing before signing any processing deal.

sections.heading: Amazon Ad Case Details Unsealed
bullets: The FTC and 22 states filed an updated complaint against Amazon with previously redacted details.
Regulators allege Amazon used deceptive and unfair practices to secretly inflate prices in its search ad auction.
The new filing points to substantial harm to advertisers, including sellers who pay for placement on Amazon.

items.title: Progress Residential and Owner Pretium Partners to Pay $49.75 Million to Settle FTC and States’ Charges Over Deceptive Rental Pricing Practices and Other Unlawful Conduct
items.snippet: The nation’s largest property manager of single-family rental homes, Progress Residential, and its owner, private equity firm Pretium Partners, will pay $49.75 million to settle charges brought by the Federal Trade Commission and four states that the companies misled consumers with deceptive rental pricing practices.
